My verdict on the frozen DG0 candidate is **PASS**, with one new Low finding that I would accept as an observation. **Candidate check.** The recomputed candidate ID matches: `sha256:c3364ac2…fb79` (commit `6c61f2e`), both in the working tree and in a fresh clone. HEAD `a733aaf` is ahead of the freeze commit by metadata commits only. The only other path they touch is `stages.json`, which is excluded from the candidate. **What I checked (15 checks; all pass, one after manual resolution)** 1. **Extraction fidelity.** I parsed the docx with my own code, independent of `tools/source`. All 1001 paragraphs appear in `playbook.md` in order, all 885 cells of the 49 tables are present, and so is the footer. `playbook.md` adds nothing except `
` line breaks. 2. **Source coverage.** All 165 playbook blocks (B0001–B0165) are correctly dispositioned (129 requirement, 29 context, 7 non-requirement). I read all 93 REQ-PB rows in full and found no dropped column, value list, rule, example, band or question. 3. **Templates.** The columns of all 16 templates (T01–T16) and every source value list are verbatim in both the register and the field inventory, with 0 problems. 4. **First-class deliverables.** All are fully specified. My strict text-matching script exited 1 with 16 misses. I checked each one by hand: all are layout differences (numbering in its own column, the thesis split into its four parts, straight instead of curly quotes), not missing content. I recorded the exit status as 1 and the result as PASS. 5. **No invented source requirements.** Every interpretation and master-prompt addition is labelled. The shipped provenance check reports 0 problems across the 93 rows. 6. **Provenance and branding.** The register presents the playbook as a practical synthesis inspired by PMI/Brightline/BRM and never as official. `#0078FF` is labelled provisional, and a provisional text wordmark is required. 7. **Operating logic.** All seven rules are stated correctly and testably: - RAG comes from the trajectory, never from task completion. - Delivery, adoption, validated value and closure are separate statuses. - A forecast never counts as validated value. - Only Finance validates, while the Business Owner stays accountable. - A shared benefit counts once, allocations are capped at 100%, and the unallocated share is shown. - Gates are explicit approvals on a frozen evidence snapshot. - DG0–DG7 stay separate from G1–G6. 8. **Master-prompt coverage.** All 423 blocks are covered. I sampled 77 blocks across all 23 sections; every disposition and mapping was correct. 9. **Staging.** Final gates follow §21 of the master prompt. 10. **Glossary, journeys and permissions.** - The Arabic terms are sensible business Arabic. - The journeys cover every phase and gate plus the other required flows. - The permissions matrix is consistent with the source roles, T11 and the RACI, and technical admins can never approve. 11. **Pre-freeze.** `prefreeze.sh DG0` passed in full (exit 0) in a fresh sandboxed clone. 12. **Earlier findings.** F-DG0-001…011 were already closed by my successful round-7 and round-9 runs, so I wrote no verifications sidecar. None of the fixes has regressed. **New finding** - **F-DG0-012 (Low, not a mandatory violation, owner `delivery-orchestrator`, requirement REQ-DLV-007).** You asked whether the new rule for skipping empty files (decision D-026) could hide a real configuration change. It can, in one narrow way. The runner's configuration scan only reports lines that are new after a run. So if a non-empty, untracked Claude config file such as `CLAUDE.local.md` is deleted, nothing is reported; that gap existed before D-026. D-026 now extends it to truncation: emptying such a file is also unreported. I reproduced both cases with the runner's own function in a disposable clone. Agents can't do this themselves, because the shell sandbox and the write guard block those paths. The gap only affects detection of a process outside the sandbox, and only for removing configuration, not adding it. It can be fixed by reporting removed lines too, and skipping an empty file only if it was absent or empty before the run. **Files** - Review record: `docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-13/domain-reviewer.json` (validates against the schema; every evidence path exists). - Findings: `docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-13/domain-reviewer.findings.json`. - Evidence logs and scripts: `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/domain/round-13/`. I removed my disposable clones afterwards.
